summary: Final-state security audit of the manual-review-workflow feature (Tasks 1-10). Zero CRITICAL / zero HIGH / zero MEDIUM findings. Seven LOW / INFO findings, all defense-in-depth or hygiene. Overall posture: clean. Safe to proceed to Pre-deploy QA (Task 14).
verdict: PASS-WITH-FINDINGS (no blocker — LOW/INFO only, all defense-in-depth / hygiene)

findings.description: `cmd_preview` unlinks `old_path = row.get('preview_html_path')` without re-validating that `Path(old_path).resolve().parent == CACHE_DIR`. If the DB were ever tampered with locally (out-of-threat-model, but defense-in-depth), a forged `preview_html_path` pointing at `/etc/something` would be deleted with operator-process privileges. The canonical write path (lines 487-497) does guard; the cleanup path does not.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the write-side path-guard in the cleanup: `p = Path(old_path).resolve(); if p.parent == CACHE_DIR: p.unlink(missing_ok=True)` — otherwise skip silently. Apply the same guard inside `_cleanup_preview_html` (hw_review.py:518-534 and news_bot.py:506-518).
findings.status: accept_or_fix (follow-up P3 — strictly local operator DB, threat model excludes DB tampering)

findings.description: `--ru-title` / `--ru-subtitle` argparse values are not run through `_validate_string_field`. A 50 KiB Russian title would be accepted and stored. The 256 KiB stdin cap + `_MAX_STRING_BYTES = 10*1024` bound the `ru_paragraphs` / `ru_blocks` payloads but not the two CLI-argv values. Since the operator is trusted this is hygiene, not an exploit.
findings.recommendation: Add `_validate_string_field(args.ru_title, '--ru-title'); _validate_string_field(args.ru_subtitle, '--ru-subtitle')` near the top of `cmd_stage` before persisting.
findings.status: accept_or_fix (follow-up P3 — operator-trusted input, no injection surface)

findings.description: `_ensure_cache_dir` uses `Path.mkdir(exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)` then `CACHE_DIR.chmod(0o700)`. `exist_ok=True` accepts a pre-existing entry regardless of whether it is a real directory, a symlink, or owned by another user. On a multi-user box (not our deployment target) this could allow a pre-planted symlink to redirect writes. The resolved `path.parent == CACHE_DIR` guard at write time (hw_review.py:491) still catches such escapes and aborts before `webbrowser.open`, so the net risk is denial-of-write plus log warning, not an XSS escape.
findings.recommendation: Optional: call `CACHE_DIR.is_dir() and not CACHE_DIR.is_symlink()` before `mkdir`, and bail if a symlink is detected. Or rely on the existing write-time path-guard (which is already correct) and add a unit test asserting the symlink case lands in the `escape cache dir` branch.
findings.status: accept (single-user operator machine — not a shared host; write-time guard defends anyway)

findings.description: `send_admin_notification` uses `parse_mode='Markdown'`. Sanitised error messages and fetched article titles may contain Markdown metacharacters (`*`, `_`, `[`, `]`, `` ` ``) that break parsing — Telegram rejects the message and the admin ping is silently lost (caught by `except TelegramError`). Observability loss, not a security hole. Pre-existing, not introduced by this feature.
findings.recommendation: Either switch to `parse_mode='MarkdownV2'` with proper escaping (requires passing every interpolated value through an escape helper), or drop `parse_mode=` entirely. Lowest-friction: drop it — admin pings don't actually need formatting.
findings.status: accept (pre-existing, not feature-introduced; admin-facing only, failure is observable via logs)

findings.description: `_SECRET_ENV_NAMES` does NOT list `GEMINI_API_KEY`. This is correct — the Gemini-LLM-transcreation feature was archived (see memory/MEMORY.md) and no code path in this feature reads `GEMINI_API_KEY`. Worth documenting for future contributors who might re-introduce an LLM-backed translator: the sanitiser tuple must be updated in lock-step.
findings.recommendation: No action. Consider adding a comment under `_SECRET_ENV_NAMES` referencing memory/MEMORY.md: 'if you add a new secret (e.g. GEMINI_API_KEY), append it here; every new secret value must be redacted before write/log.'

findings.description: `logger.error(f"list_pending failed: {exc}")` and `logger.error(f"Failed to send admin ping: {notify_err}")` in `job()` step (6) do NOT run through `sanitize_error_message`. Every other error path in `job()` / `_fallback_publish` / `_overflow_fast_track` DOES. If `list_pending` raised a sqlite error embedding a token (implausible — `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` is never in a SQL string), the value would leak to logs. Risk is theoretical; worth tightening for uniformity.
findings.recommendation: Wrap both: `logger.error(f"list_pending failed: {sanitize_error_message(exc)}")` and `logger.error(f"Failed to send admin ping: {sanitize_error_message(notify_err)}")` to match the pattern used everywhere else in the same function.
findings.status: info (cosmetic uniformity; no realistic secret-leak vector)

findings.description: `_loads_or_none` uses `json.loads(raw)` without a max-depth / max-size guard. A manually-tampered DB row containing e.g. 5 MiB of `[[[[[...]]]]` could cause stack-overflow or memory spike on deserialisation. Threat model: DB is local-only, operator-trusted, so this is not a production risk. Noting for completeness.
findings.recommendation: No action for this milestone. If the DB ever becomes shared or writeable by an untrusted process, add a `len(raw) < N MiB` precheck or switch to `json.loads(..., parse_constant=...)` with a depth cap wrapper.

invariants_check.evidence: `grep -nE "execute\(\s*f|execute\(\s*[\"'][^\"']*%|\.format\s*\(" pending_articles_repo.py` → empty. Each execute() call across pending_articles_repo.py:156-657 passes a tuple as the 2nd arg.

news_bot.py:762 `pending_repo.increment_attempt(link, safe)` with `safe = sanitize_error_message(exc)`; news_bot.py:771,1025 `move_to_failed(_link, safe)`; news_bot.py:1016 idle-fallback mirror. Only `increment_attempt` / `move_to_failed` write `last_error`, both receive pre-sanitised `safe`.

preview_renderer.py:65 `_SAFE_URL_RE = re.compile(r'^https?://', re.IGNORECASE)`; preview_renderer.py:77-81 `_CSP_META` contains exact `default-src 'none'; img-src https:; frame-src https:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'`; preview_renderer.py:73 `_SAFE_ATTR_NAME_RE` closes the round-2 attribute-name-injection hole.

hw_review.py:487 `path = Path(tmp.name).resolve()`; hw_review.py:491 `if path.parent != CACHE_DIR: ... return 1`. webbrowser.open at hw_review.py:506 only reached when the guard passes. CACHE_DIR itself is `Path('~/.cache/hw-review/').expanduser().resolve()` at module load (line 92), so the comparison is between two canonical resolved paths.

(1) 256 KiB stdin cap: hw_review.py:336-343 `sys.stdin.buffer.read(_STDIN_READ_LIMIT)` then `if len(raw) >= _STDIN_READ_LIMIT: reject`. (2) depth > 3: _validate_depth at hw_review.py:254-264. (3) unknown top keys: hw_review.py:302-312. (4) non-list ru_paragraphs: hw_review.py:317-318. (5) non-dict block entries: hw_review.py:275-276. (6) unknown block type: hw_review.py:278-279. (7) unknown block keys: hw_review.py:281-283. (8) string field > 10 KiB: hw_review.py:267-271 _validate_string_field.

owasp_walkthrough.A01_access_control: PASS. Operator-only CLI; no remote-trust surface. `hw_review publish N` resolves `N` via `_resolve_pending` (1-based list of pending rows) — cannot address a row outside pending_articles. `retry N` is a 1-based list_failed index; cannot address pending or published. No UID spoofing path.
owasp_walkthrough.A02_crypto_failures: PASS. `_SECRET_ENV_NAMES` covers TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN / TELEGRAM_CHANNEL_ID / TELEGRAM_ADMIN_ID / TELEGRAPH_ACCESS_TOKEN. Empty-env-var pathology closed at news_bot.py:88 (`if not value or not value.strip(): continue`). `sanitize_error_message` called on every exception before write/admin-ping in `_fallback_publish`, `_overflow_fast_track`, `cmd_publish`, and job() error paths (news_bot.py:762,771,1016,1025 / hw_review.py:580,607). `TelegraphError` messages reference field names not values (telegraph_publisher.py:43,289). `requests` exceptions do not embed the token (token is in POST body, not URL).
owasp_walkthrough.A03_injection: PASS. (SQL) All pending_articles_repo.py queries use `?` placeholders — grep-verified. The `list_pending_stale(hours)` / `list_notified_overdue(grace_hours)` construct a string fragment `f'-{int(hours)}'` for SQLite's `datetime(..., ?)` modifier — but `int()` coercion makes injection impossible even if a caller passed a hostile string. (Command) `webbrowser.open(f"file://{path}")` where `path` is a resolved `Path` inside CACHE_DIR with `uuid4`-like prefix from `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile` — no shell interpolation. (JSON) `stage N` validator rejects malformed / oversized / deep / unknown-key payloads before touching the DB.
owasp_walkthrough.A04_insecure_design: PASS. Prep-phase / publish-phase split is the core design invariant — enforced. Staged-row protection is pushed down to `ru_paragraphs IS NULL` in the SQL WHERE clauses of `list_notified_overdue` (pending_articles_repo.py:407) and `list_pending_for_eviction` (pending_articles_repo.py:426), eliminating a SELECT+Python-filter+DELETE race window. Decision-9 idempotency (persist `telegraph_url` BEFORE teaser step) closes the double-publish race. Per-row try/except around `_fallback_publish` prevents one row's failure from aborting the pass.
owasp_walkthrough.A05_security_misconfiguration: PASS. CSP meta is exact and byte-compared in tests. Tag allowlist, URL-scheme allowlist (`^https?://` IGNORECASE), attribute-name allowlist (`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$`) all in place. CACHE_DIR is `0o700` via both `mkdir(mode=0o700)` AND defensive `chmod(0o700)`. Script runs as the operator user, not root.
owasp_walkthrough.A06_vulnerable_components: PASS (at time of audit). requirements.txt: `feedparser==6.0.10` / `requests==2.32.3` / `beautifulsoup4==4.12.3` / `deep-translator==1.11.4` / `schedule==1.2.1` / `python-telegram-bot==21.10` / `curl_cffi==0.15.0`. All pinned. `requests==2.32.3` is the CVE-2024-35195-patched release. No stdlib-breaking pins. Recommend scheduling a quarterly `pip-audit` as standard hygiene — out-of-scope for this feature.
owasp_walkthrough.A07_auth_failures: N/A. Operator-only local CLI; no login flow, no session management, no password storage. Telegram bot token and Telegraph access token authenticate the outbound API calls; token handling is covered under A02.
owasp_walkthrough.A08_data_integrity: PASS. JSON (de)serialisation uses `ensure_ascii=False` (pending_articles_repo.py:111-117) — Cyrillic round-trips without `\uXXXX`. Transactional moves use explicit try/commit/rollback/close (pending_articles_repo.py:480-525, 533-566, 574-599, 612-657). Decision 9 trusts the stored `telegraph_url` on retry — legitimate because the process itself wrote it; DB tamper is out of threat model.
owasp_walkthrough.A09_logging_monitoring: PASS with INFO-level non-uniformities (see findings). Every write-path to pending_articles.last_error / failed_articles.last_error passes through `sanitize_error_message`. Admin-ping composition is size-bounded (integer counts in overflow ping; titles-only in idle heads-up — admin's own Telegram will truncate oversized messages). `send_admin_notification`'s TelegramError catch (news_bot.py:109-111) swallows failure — correct behaviour for a notifier, but noted for observability.
owasp_walkthrough.A10_ssrf: PASS. No user-controlled URL reaches a server-side HTTP call. `webbrowser.open` opens a local `file://` URL. RSS fetch URLs come from `feeds.json` (operator-edited) with `urlparse(item).scheme in ('http', 'https')` guard at news_bot.py:146. `send_telegraph_teaser` sends to the hard-coded `TELEGRAM_CHANNEL_ID`. `telegraph_publisher._api_call` posts to the hard-coded `API_BASE = 'https://api.telegra.ph'`.

feature_specific_checks.secret_exposure_hw_review_show: PASS. `cmd_show` prints `row.get('last_error')` which was already sanitised at write time (Decision 11). `telegraph_url` is printed raw but never contains a token (Telegra.ph URLs are public). No re-desanitisation loop.
feature_specific_checks.cyrillic_encoding: PASS. `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False)` preserves Cyrillic in DB TEXT columns. `html.escape(..., quote=True)` on every string leaf preserves Cyrillic bytes while neutralising HTML-special chars. Attribute values pass through the same escape. Sanitiser's `str.replace(value, '[REDACTED]')` works unicode-correctly since it compares raw bytes of a unicode str — a Cyrillic error string containing a token substring redacts correctly.
feature_specific_checks.symlink_toctou_preview_cache: PASS with one LOW finding (see finding #1). Write-time path-guard (hw_review.py:491) compares `Path(tmp.name).resolve().parent` to CACHE_DIR (also resolved at import). A mid-flight symlink planted under CACHE_DIR would cause the resolved tmp-file path to land outside CACHE_DIR, triggering the escape branch — `_err('preview path escaped cache dir')` + return 1 — which aborts BEFORE `set_preview_path` and BEFORE `webbrowser.open`.
feature_specific_checks.telegraph_token_in_network_errors: PASS. `publish_article` → `_api_call` → `requests.post(url, data={'access_token': token, ...})`. `requests.exceptions.HTTPError` / `Timeout` / `ConnectionError` strings contain the URL and status, not the POST body. `TelegraphError` raises `f"{method} failed: {body.get('error')}"` — Telegraph's API error field references parameter names, never the token value. Sanitiser is belt-and-braces correct regardless.
feature_specific_checks.empty_env_var_pathology: PASS. news_bot.py:88 `if not value or not value.strip(): continue` guards against the `str.replace('', '[REDACTED]')` interleaving pathology. Covered by tests/test_admin_ping.py.
feature_specific_checks.overflow_eviction_race: PASS. `list_pending_for_eviction` applies `WHERE ru_paragraphs IS NULL` in SQL (pending_articles_repo.py:426) — staged rows can never appear in the eviction candidate list, even under concurrent `hw_review stage N`. No SELECT+DELETE race window.
